_comment: THE DECK-OUT KILL OFF AN ASSEMBLED BLINK LOOP -- the drain fixture's twin, with Dimensional
Infiltrator ('{1}{C}: Target opponent exiles the top card of their library') as the sink. Same
Emiel / Peregrine Drake board, same four lands worth seven mana a tap. Twelve cards left in
their library, which is 24 mana at {1}{C} apiece -- three and a half times what the board makes
in a turn, so ONLY the loop can pay for it.
Two things this pins that the drain fixture cannot:
1. ALL OR NOTHING. Exiling is worth nothing until the library is empty -- 11 of 12 wins exactly
as often as 0 -- so SpendSurplusOnExile pays for the whole library in ONE scaled payment and
otherwise spends not a single mana. An earlier version guarded with a flat-pool projection
(AvailableManaPool + float vs CanPay) and that is not good enough: it passed on a board with
six colourless in the flat sense, then the sequential payments realised only five and it
exiled 5 of 6, throwing ten mana away for nothing.
2. THE COLOURLESS HOLD. Twelve {C} pips are needed SIMULTANEOUSLY and this board makes three
colourless per untap, so they have to be banked as float across iterations -- but generic
pips take colourless ahead of any colour by default, so the blink's own {3} eats them as
fast as the tap-ahead makes them. g_hold_colorless_for_pips moves colourless to the back of
the generic order for the duration of a loop that has this sink on board. Measured on this
fixture: without the hold it is win_turn 6, with it 4.
DISCRIMINATING: at opponent_library_size 20 the mana genuinely does not reach and the engine
correctly falls back to win_turn 5. The threshold is where it should be, not at infinity.
